correctness.rationale: An m-letter tuple of reversible d-dimensional transitions first becomes two reversible operators A,B on r=m-1 copies: A cycles with the first transition on wrap, B acts by the other transitions on indexed copies. The signed macros a^r and a^j b a^-j preserve a fixed core and implement all original letters exactly. An explicit six-copy gadget has positive binary generators S,T satisfying S^2=T^3=I and implements A,A^-1,B,B^-1 via stst, ttstts, sttstt,tsts, respectively, each preserving the core. Hence all original words have exact compiled positive binary counterparts, dimension factor 6(m-1), word-length factor L_m=max[4(m-1),10(m-2)+6]. For m=4 this is D factor18 and horizon factor26, so the cited four-letter identification lower bounds become binary with the same asymptotic exponents, and general two-letter packing bounds match. Distinct-prefix/suffix conditions survive strict diagonal/off-diagonal acceptance margin. If lambda2=0, source four-letter logarithmic-D law similarly transfers; unary N<=T+1 cannot attain the positive-tolerance exponential-in-T scaling at D=T. Independent permutation tracking checked 60 exact letter-actions over 15 dimension/alphabet families, including inverse implementation and length bounds. The core algebra proves arbitrary unitaries, not numerical samples.
